 J U D G M E N T

The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 8.1.2016 at about 11.30 p.m. the petitioner was a pedestrian walking on the left s i d e o f t h e r o a d , w h e n s h e r e a c h e d T h y a m a g o n d l u - B e g a r u r o a d ,
Hanumanthegowdanapalya, Thyamagondlu hobli, Nelamangala, Bengaluru, at that time one tempo traveler bearing NO.KA-52-A-3666 driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the petitioner.
Consequent to the terrific impact, the petitioner was fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately she was shifted to Mathrushree hospital, Nelamangala, Bengaluru wherein she took the treatment as an inpatient.

3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy,
aged about 8 years, student.
On account of the injuries she could not attend the class.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tempo Traveller.

Therefore,
respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

Contending the above facts,
she prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.

4. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court, placed exparte and the respondent No.2 has appeared before the court and filed its respective written statement.

5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent No.2 in its written statement averred that, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied mandatory provisions u/s 134 and S.158 (6) of the MV Act.
Further admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-51-C-8214 and its validity.
Further contended that the person driving the vehicle has no relation in force as on the date of accident to drive the vehicle.
Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the above said vehicle as on the date of accident.
Further contended that the insured tempo traveler has no permit to ply the vehicle in a place of accident.
Further contended that tempo traveler bearing No.KA-52-A-3666 is not at all involved in the accident.

Further denied the age avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim Kumari Lavanya vs Shri Byregowda on 3 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128907514/
2 petition.
Contending the above facts, prays to dismiss the claim petition with cost.
6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tempo Traveler bearing registration No.KA-52-A- 3666 on 8.1.2018 at about 11.30 p.m. near Hanumanthegowdanapalya , on Thyamagondlu- Beguru road, Thyamagondlu Hobli, Nelamangala, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case, the father of the petitioner has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P13.

8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 has examined Thyamagondlu Head constable as RW1 and got marked the document at Ex.R1, official of RTO is examined as RW2 and got marked the document at Ex.R2 & Ex.R3 and respondent No.2 examined its Legal Manager as RW3 and got marked the document at Ex.R4.

9. Heard the arguments.
10.

My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S 11. ISSUE NO.1:- During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1.
Further he argued that, the petitioner has proved her case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued by denying the manner of the accident as alleged in the petition and contended that the alleged vehicle was not at all involved in the accident.
Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.2.
13. On rival contention urged by both the counsel, I, intend to discuss the merits of the case.

3 14.
In order to prove the case, the father of the petitioner has examined as P.W.1 and he has stated in his evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.
To substantiate the said contention he has produced prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P4 and Ex.
P7 such as FIR with Complaint, spot mahazar, seizure mahazar, IMV report and charge sheet respectively.
15. On perusal of complaint marked at Ex.P1 reveals that, complaint has been lodged by the father of the petitioner Venkatesh on 8.1.2018.
Based on the complaint FIR marked at Ex.P1 has been registered against the driver of the Tempo traveller in Cr.No.4/2018 by Thyamagondlu police for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P2 is the spot mahazar also reveals scene of occurrence.
Ex.P3 is seizure mahazar also shows that after the accident vehicle has been seized.
IMV report at Ex.P4 also reveals the damages caused to the vehicle and IMV inspector has opined that accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defect of the vehicle.

On perusal of charge sheet at Ex.P6 reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the offending vehicle driver for the offences punishable U/s 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
16.
The counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued that the alleged vehicle was not at all involved in the accident.

To substantiate the said fact, he has examined Head constable, Thyamagondlu as RW1,
but his evidence will not help the respondent No.2 to prove his defence.
17. Though, the respondent No.2 has cross-examined the PW1 at length, but nothing worth material has been elicited from him.

18. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).
19.

sentences.text: Looking to the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court I am of the opinion that, petitioner has proved her case that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tempo Traveller bearing registration No.KA-52-A-3666.
Hence, I answer this issue in the affirmative.

20. ISSUE NO.2:- PW1 being the father of the petitioner has stated in his evidence that petitioner has met with an accident on 8.1.2018 at about 11.30 a.m. and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately she was taken to Mathrushree hospital, wherein she took treatment inpatient.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor.

Considering the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony, for which, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of pain Kumari Lavanya vs Shri Byregowda on 3 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128907514/
4
and sufferings.
22. The case of the petitioner is that, she was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 8 years.
Due to the accidental injuries she has suffered a lot.
PW1 has produced discharge summaries marked at Ex.P5 & Ex.P6, which reveals that the petitioner was admitted on 8.1.2018 and discharged on 10.1.2018.
During the said period either father or mother, one has to look after their daughter by leaving their work.
So, I deem it fit to grant Rs.15,000/- under the head of inconvenience caused to the parents during the treatment period.
Therefore, Rs.15,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.
23. The contention of PW1 is that, they have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses.

He has produced the medical bills at Ex.P9 to the extent of Rs.17,553/- supported with prescriptions, hence,
I deem it just and reasonable to grant compensation of Rs.17,553/- under the head of medical expenses.

24. Further contention of the PW1 is that, prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy,
aged about 8 years, student.
Due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and do normal activities.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to speak about the grievousness of the injuries or to assess the disability.
Therefore, no amount is granted for disability.
25. PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accident petitioner took the treatment as inpatient and also as outpatient.
On perusal of Ex.P5 discharge summary, which reveals that the petitioner was admitted on 8.1.2018 and discharged on 10.1.2018.
So, one must attend her during the above said period.

So, considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.10,000/-under the head of amenities, attendant, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.,
26.

Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
Sl.No. Compensation heads Amount 1. Pain and suffering Rs. 30,000-00 2. Loss of income during laid period Rs. 15,000-00 and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs. 17,553-00 4. Loss of amenities, Attendant, Rs. 10,000-00 Nourishment and conveyance charges Total Rs.72,553-00 27.

LIABILITY: As I have already discussed in issue No.1 that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tempo traveler bearing No.KA-52-A-3666.
28.
The counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued that as on the date of accident the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving license to drive the said vehicle.

The respondent has issued commercial vehicle package policy to the tempo traveler, but the driver was not holding Kumari Lavanya vs Shri Byregowda on 3 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128907514/
5 the driving license to drive the same.
To substantiate the said fact, the respondent No.2 has examined official of the RTO office as RW2.
He has produced the authorization letter at Ex.R1 and driving license extract at Ex.R3.
29 . Further the respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW3, he has reiterated the similar facts as stated in the written statement.
He has produced insurance policy, which is marked at Ex.R4.
The petitioner has cross-examined RW2, he has admitted that the unladen weight of the insured vehicle is less than 7500.

on perusal of Ex.R4, it shows that CC/HP 2596, make/model and variant is force motors/traveler and Mini bus 3350 Wb.
30.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On perusal of the same, it is observed that a person holding driving licence to drive 'light motor vehicle' is competent to drive transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7,500 kgs or a motor car or tractor or road roller, the unladen weight of which does not exceed 7,500 kg.
32. In the instant case the driver of the offending vehicle can drive transport vehicle, the gross vehicle weight of below 7500 kgs.
Therefore, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 holds no water.
33. The respondent No.2 has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of Tempo traveler bearing No. KA-52-A-3666 and its validity.
Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in the partly affirmative.
34. ISSUE NO.3:

sentences.text: The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of MV Act as against the respondents is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.72,553/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount together with interest, entire amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any nationalized/schedule bank till she attains age of majority and after attaining the age of majority the entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through e-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer online, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this 3rd day of February 2020).
